judged_text: The new Salesforce token refresh plus prisma.credential.update runs unconditionally on every jsforce connection creation — unlike every other refresh path in this diff, it is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. All existing non-sharing Salesforce users now pay an extra synchronous OAuth round-trip plus DB write per service instantiation, and any Salesforce or network failure during the refresh throws HttpError and aborts calendar operations that previously succeeded using the still-valid stored token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`) and an unconditional `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no check for token expiry and no feature-flag gating (e.g., `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`), so every service instantiation now performs a network OAuth round-trip and DB write; additionally, failures throw (`HttpError` on non-OK `statusText`) and can abort calendar operations even if the previously stored access token might still be usable.
